questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
questions.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{2}}{4}+18,\,\frac{(2t-1)(t+8)}{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{2}}{4}+18),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{(2t-1)(t+8)}{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{2\cdot (t+8)+(2t-1)\cdot 1}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{4t+15}{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4t+15}{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
questions.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨4(t+2)^{5/2},3t-2⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4(t+2)^{5/2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨10(t+2)^{3/2},3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(10(t+2)^{3/2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨15(t+2)^{1/2},0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨15(2+2)^{1/2},0⟩ \\  & =⟨15\sqrt{4},0⟩ \\  & =⟨15(2),0⟩ \\  & =⟨30,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(2)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(2)| & =|⟨30,0⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(30)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =30\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\frac{6}{t},\,3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(3)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{6}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{6}{{t}^{2}},\,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨-\frac{6}{(3)^{2}},\,6(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{6}{9},\,18⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{3},\,18⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{e}^{3t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,3{e}^{3t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{3t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,9{e}^{3t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+5,\,6+{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(3)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6+{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-4t,\,3{t}^{2}-8t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t-4,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨6(3)-4,\,6(3)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨14,\,10⟩\end{aligned}
$$
